feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so it states no outcome for it. Iteration 1 (7 sensors, 16 mm, y=0.05, wheel_track 0.12, kp 1.5, kd 0.25) is the best base: 55.1, with line loss 0 on the oval, 0.6 on the s-bend and 1.0 on the slalom. All 60 trials per iteration still ended off_track with max_error at the 0.06 m floor, so turn authority is the open question. Iteration 2 (y=0.07, shorter and lighter body) dropped to 47.8, with s-bend progress falling from 0.163 to 0.119, so yaw inertia and sensor lead did not help. I have kept the iteration 1 controller so the wheel_track change is isolated. When the next race reports, use these rules. If max_error falls below 0.06 m with progress above 0.15 and steering_oscillation stays near 0.15 or below, narrow wheel_track further to 0.08 m. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.15 on the s-bend or slalom, the extra turn rate is overshooting: keep wheel_track at 0.09 m and I will lower kp rather than change geometry. If progress stays near 0.12 with max_error unchanged, the limit is speed, not turn rate, so the next geometry test is wheel_radius.
requested_changes: If max_error drops below 0.06 m on the s-bend and slalom with steering_oscillation at or below about 0.15: try wheel_track 0.08 m (the contract minimum). Evidence: iteration 1 max_error was 0.0648 on the s-bend and 0.0665 on the slalom, both at the off-track floor, and this change tests whether more turn rate per unit of differential helps.

If progress stays near 0.12 with max_error still at 0.06 m and no change in line loss: change wheel_radius from 0.03 m to 0.035 m for more ground speed, keeping wheel_track at 0.09 m. Evidence: iteration 1 progress was 0.112 to 0.163 on all tracks with no sign of turn-rate gain, so speed may be the limit.

If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.15 on the s-bend or slalom: return wheel_track to 0.12 m and raise mass from 0.8 kg to 0.9 kg before changing the sensors. Evidence: iteration 1 steering_oscillation was 0.150 on the s-bend and 0.161 on the slalom, and iteration 2's lighter body (mass 0.6 kg) pushed the s-bend score down, so extra inertia should be tested before more sensor lead.
